_comment: Manually-maintained Australian Competition Tribunal appeal data, keyed by ACCC merger_id. Merged into the frontend data by scripts/static_data (see loaders.load_tribunal_appeals and enrichment.link_tribunal_appeals). IMPORTANT: an entry here does NOT by itself make a merger 'under appeal' — a matter stays listed after it finishes. A merger is shown as under appeal only while 'status' is 'current' (anything other than 'concluded' counts as current; a finished/withdrawn appeal must be marked 'concluded'). Fields: tribunal_number (e.g. 'ACT 1 of 2026'), tribunal_url (the tribunal matter page), appeal_type (one of party_denial / party_conditional_clearance / third_party_clearance — see scripts/constants/tribunal.py), appellant (who lodged the review), status ('current' | 'concluded'), filed_date, hearing_date (optional; the date the tribunal hearing starts, as a bare ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' — while the appeal is current and the date is still in the future it is surfaced as a 'Tribunal hearing' upcoming/tracked event, exempt from the usual look-ahead window since a hearing is scheduled months in advance), and documents[] which are folded into the merger's event timeline regardless of status. Once concluded, also set: outcome (one of affirmed / set_aside / varied / withdrawn / dismissed), effective_determination (the ACCC-style determination that now stands — same as the ACCC's when affirmed, the opposite when set aside, e.g. 'Approved' / 'Not approved' — used to render the status badge like 'Approved · on appeal'), and concluded_date. Each document: date, filed_by, description, confidentiality ('Confidential' | 'Non-confidential'), url (direct tribunal link, treated like an ACCC url), optionally url_gh (local mirror served from data/raw/matters/{id}/), and optionally section (the H3 heading a document was listed under, e.g. 'Submissions by interested party'; absent for the main first table). The documents[] list is populated from the live tribunal matter pages by scripts/scrape_tribunal.py (run via the 'Scrape Tribunal' workflow), which uses each entry's tribunal_url as the page to scrape, downloads each linked file into data/raw/matters/{merger_id}/ and sets its url_gh serve path automatically; every other field here is still maintained by hand.
